stories.headline: Hyderabad police heighten security after email warns of terror attack
stories.title: Hyderabad police heighten security after email warns of terror attack
stories.summary: Hyderabad police have intensified security measures after receiving an email warning of terror attacks modelled on the 2008 Mumbai attacks and allegedly linked to Lashkar-e-Taiba. The message threatened twin bomb blasts, claimed the attacks were in retaliation for the killing of LeT operative Lateef Bhat.

stories.headline: Govt following 'zero-casualty' approach for disaster management: Amit Shah
stories.title: Govt following 'zero-casualty' approach for disaster management: Amit Shah
stories.summary: Itanagar, Nov 22: Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Sunday said the government was following a 'zero-casualty' approach for disaster management, under which timely warnings and immediate evacuation measures were being prioritised to protect vulnerable people. Inaugurating the 12th battalion campus of the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) at Hollongi, near here, he said it would significantly strengthen disaster preparedness and response across the Northeast, one of the country's most vulnerable regions to natural calamities. Shah said the region is prone to various natural disasters and stressed the need for preparedness, modern warning systems and coordinated efforts to minimise loss of lives and property. He said the campus has been constructed in accordance with earthquake-resistant standards, keeping in view the vulnerability of the region to seismic activity. The home minister said the NDRF's expansion, improvement in resources and specialised training were among the key priorities of the government to strengthen the country's disaster management capabilities. Highlighting the importance of community participation in disaster management, the home minister appreciated the role of local volunteers, including children associated with scouts and trained 'Aapda Mitras', who remain prepared to assist people during emergencies. He said disaster management efforts should not be limited to specialised forces but must involve people at the grassroots level, including village-level functionaries.

stories.headline: Supreme Court To Examine Whether Former Mutawalli Can Represent Waqf As Sajjadanashin After Tenure Ends
stories.title: Supreme Court To Examine Whether Former Mutawalli Can Represent Waqf As Sajjadanashin After Tenure Ends
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has agreed to examine the question of whether a former Mutawalli (caretaker of waqf) can continue representing a Waqf in legal proceedings after the expiry of his tenure by claiming that he is also a Sajjadanashin (spiritual head of a shrine).

A Bench of Justice Manoj Misra and Justice Vijay Bishnoi was hearing a plea challenging the Karnataka High Court's Kalaburagi Bench judgment, which allowed a suit filed by the Dargah to continue through a Waqf Officer after the petitioner's tenure as Mutawalli expired.

The dispute arose after the Waqf Tribunal dismissed the Dargah's suit seeking a declaration that certain properties were Waqf properties, on the ground that the person representing it no longer held the position of Mutawalli.
The High Court set aside the dismissal, holding that the suit had been instituted in the name of the Waqf institution and should not fail merely because its Mutawalli's tenure had ended.
It directed that the proceedings continue through the Waqf Officer.

Before the Supreme Court, the petitioner challenging the High Court's judgment argued that he could continue representing the Dargah because he was also a Sajjadanashin, an office which does not carry a fixed tenure.

The Court observed that the issue was whether, in the absence of a Waqfnama or any custom pleaded in the original proceedings establishing the petitioner's position as Sajjadanashin, he could continue representing the Dargah after his appointment as Mutawalli had expired.

“What is relevant to be considered is whether in absence of any Waqfnama or a Waqf deed, and in absence of any custom pleaded in the plaint/application preferred before the Tribunal by the petitioner of him being the Sajjadanashin of the Dargah concerned, having accepted his appointment as a Mutawalli, could he continue to represent the Waqf/Dargah on expiry of his term as the Mutawalli.”, the Court noted.
For deciding the issue, the bench has listed the matter for further hearing on November 25, seeking assistance from the petitioner's counsel.
